items.body: Your retirement "plan" is a stack of 401(k)s, IRAs, and brokerage accounts with a vague target date — no real income strategy and no proof it survives a downturn.

items.body: If a major market drop hits right as you retire, you could be forced to sell low. Most people have no idea how much risk they're actually carrying.

items.title: Fees, Taxes & No Coordination

faqs.q: I already have a financial advisor. Why do I need this?
faqs.a: Most clients do. The difference is coordination: we stress-test your income, audit fees and taxes, and tie investments, insurance, and estate together — the questions a "money manager" rarely answers.

faqs.q: Is this a sales pitch for products?
faqs.a: No. We're fiduciaries. The assessment and review are educational; any recommendation is based on what's right for your plan, never a commission.

faqs.q: What is the Retirement Red Zone Stress Test?
faqs.a: It shows how your accounts and withdrawal plan would hold up if a major market drop hit early in retirement — so you understand your real risk before it matters.

faqs.q: How much do I need to get started?
faqs.a: We typically work with households with $2M–$10M in investable assets, though the right fit always depends on your specific situation and goals.

faqs.q: What does being a fiduciary mean?
faqs.a: We're legally and ethically required to act in your best interest — coordinating your full plan rather than selling products.

faqs.q: How quickly will someone follow up?
faqs.a: If you qualify, a fiduciary specialist typically reaches out within one business day to schedule your strategy session.
